0.headline: Jindal Supreme IPO booked over 20x so far on Day 2; GMP soars to 30%
0.heading: Jindal Supreme IPO booked over 20x so far on Day 2; GMP soars to 30%
0.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of steel pipes and tubes maker Jindal Supreme India continued to attract strong investor interest on the second day of bidding, with the issue subscribed 20.20 times as of 1:40 pm on September 17, according to NSE data.
0.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of steel pipes and tubes maker Jindal Supreme India continued to attract strong investor interest on the second day of bidding, with the issue subscribed 20.20 times as of 1:40 pm on September 17, according to NSE data.

The Rs 124.88 crore IPO received bids for nearly 19 crore shares, against 93.99 lakh shares on offer. The retail portion was subscribed 28.39 times, while the non-institutional investor (NII) portion was booked 20.79 times. The issue opened for subscription on September 16 and will close on September 18.

In the grey market, Jindal Supreme shares are commanding a premium of around 30 percent over the upper end of the IPO price band, according to InvestorGain.

Read Also: NSE IPO subscribed 30% so far on Day 1; should you apply?

The company has fixed the price band for the IPO at Rs 88-93 per share. At the upper end of the price band, a 30 percent GMP translates into a premium of around Rs 28 per share, indicating a possible listing price of around Rs 121, if the grey market trend holds.

However, grey market premium (GMP) is an unofficial indicator and can change before listing.

Ahead of the public issue, Jindal Supreme India mobilised Rs 37.46 crore through its anchor book by issuing 40.28 lakh shares on September 15.

Three investors participated in the anchor book, with Craft Emerging Market Fund PCC emerging as the largest investor.

Craft Emerging Market Fund PCC, through its three schemes — Arbitrage Strategy Fund, Citadel Capital Fund and Elite Capital Fund — acquired 29.53 lakh shares for Rs 27.46 crore at the upper end of the price band.

Minerva Emerging Opportunities Fund and Ekamya Pragati Scheme each acquired 5.37 lakh shares for Rs 5 crore.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of 1.07 crore equity shares and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 26.86 lakh shares by promoter entity VVJ Enterprise.

Jindal Supreme India manufactures mild steel black pipes and tubes, galvanised pipes, metal beam crash barriers and galvanised iron tubular poles. Its products are used in water supply and plumbing, infrastructure and construction, roads and highways, bridges, oil and gas, chemicals, agriculture and rural electrification.

The company plans to use Rs 71 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue towards repayment or prepayment of debt. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

As of June 2026, Jindal Supreme India had total borrowings of Rs 92.46 crore, along with accrued interest on borrowings.

Check IPO News Here

Jindal Supreme India reported a profit of Rs 8.3 crore and revenue of Rs 190.93 crore for the quarter ended June 2026.

For the financial year ended March 2026, the company's profit declined 7.2 percent to Rs 22.5 crore from Rs 24.3 crore in the previous year. Revenue, however, increased 15.2 percent to Rs 675.4 crore from Rs 586.4 crore.

The IPO is being managed by Sarthi Capital Advisors, which is acting as the merchant banker to the issue.

The shares are proposed to be listed on both the BSE and NSE.

1.headline: NSE IPO Opens Today: Decoding Strengths, Concerns & Valuation | IPO Street
1.heading: NSE IPO Opens Today: Decoding Strengths, Concerns & Valuation | IPO Street
1.intro: Neha Dave, Special Analyst at MC Pro, joins Moneycontrol's IPO Street to break down everything investors need to know about the National Stock Exchange's much-awaited IPO, which opens for subscription today. Dave walks through the issue details — a ₹22,562-crore offer for sale with a price band of ₹1,700-1,785, valuing NSE at ₹4.42 lakh crore at the upper end. She discusses the exchange's key strengths, including its durable business model, high entry barriers, network effect moat, and position as a direct proxy to India's financialisation story. Dave also flags the key concerns, from heavy reliance on transaction income to regulatory tightening risks around equity options volumes. She rounds off with MC Pro's valuation take and shares whether long-term investors should consider subscribing to the issue.

2.headline: SS Retail IPO subscribed nearly 3x so far on second day; GMP at 28%
2.heading: SS Retail IPO subscribed nearly 3x so far on second day; GMP at 28%
2.intro: The initial pubic offering (IPO) of multi-brand mobile retail chain SS Retail remained in demand on the second day of bidding, with the issue receiving 2.71 times subscription, as of 12:15 pm on September 17, according to NSE data.
2.body:
The initial pubic offering (IPO) of multi-brand mobile retail chain SS Retail remained in demand on the second day of bidding, with the issue receiving 2.71 times subscription, as of 12:15 pm on September 17, according to NSE data.

The Rs 500-crore IPO received bids for 2,38,05,145 shares against 87,93,884 shares on offer. The retail investor portion was subscribed 4.04 times, while the non-institutional investor (NII) category was booked 3.31 times.

In the grey market, SS Retail shares were commanding a premium of around 28 percent over the upper end of the IPO price band, according to InvestorGain. Investors must note that the grey market premiums are unofficial indicators and can change before listing.

The Rs 500-crore IPO will remain open for subscription until September 18. The issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 360 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of Rs 140 crore. The price band has been fixed at Rs 403-424 per share.

Ahead of the public issue, SS Retail raised Rs 146.4 crore from anchor investors through the allotment of 34.52 lakh shares to 14 institutional investors at Rs 424 per share.

Read Also: Hero Motors IPO: Issue subscribed over 2x on Day 2 so far; GMP at 16%

Domestic mutual funds accounted for a significant portion of the anchor allocation. SS Retail allotted 28.70 lakh shares, or 83.14 percent of the total anchor book, to 11 domestic mutual funds through 19 schemes.

The investors included SBI Mutual Fund, Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company, Axis Mutual Fund, WhiteOak Capital, Motilal Oswal Asset Management Company, Invesco and Aditya Birla Sun Life Asset Management Company.

Bengal Finance and Investment, backed by investor Ashish Kacholia, Kotak Mahindra Life Insurance and 360 ONE were also among the anchor investors. The three investors collectively invested nearly Rs 25 crore in the issue.

SS Retail plans to use a substantial portion of the fresh issue proceeds towards funding its working capital requirements.

Of the net proceeds from the fresh issue, Rs 241.3 crore has been earmarked for incremental working capital requirements, while Rs 12.4 crore will be used for setting up new stores during the current financial year and FY28. The remaining funds will be deployed towards general corporate purposes.

The company plans to add 120 stores each in FY27 and FY28. Between April and July 2026, SS Retail had already added 33 stores.

For the planned store expansion, the company intends to spend up to Rs 5.81 crore on 57 stores in FY27 and up to Rs 6.64 crore on 58 stores in FY28.

Check IPO News Here

SS Retail operates a multi-brand retail chain selling mobile phones, accessories and other electronic products. Its operations span Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Goa and Gujarat.

As of July 31, 2026, the company had expanded its retail network to 536 stores across these five states. As of March 31, 2026, it operated 503 stores.

The IPO is being managed by Anand Rathi Advisors and Emkay Global Financial Services as the book-running lead managers. SS Retail's shares are scheduled to be listed on the NSE and BSE on September 23, subject to the completion of the IPO process.
